sources.summary: Printout of OPS-ADE action 609617, a modification of the operation notification for data centres, status 'Οριστικά Υποβληθείσα' (finally submitted) on 20/10/2026 15:10, by economic operator DATA 4 GREECE Μονοπρόσωπη Α.Ε. The data centre provides services to third parties; declared total nominal IT-equipment power 6,000 kW and main-space area 8,908.42 m2. Field 18 states that the total area of the spaces that have been completed and for which Construction Inspection Certificate (Π.Ε.Κ.) no. 2688/08-07-2026 has been issued is 8,908.42 m2, and that the notification concerns part of building K1 (DC01 data centre, 8,550.85 m2: part of the basement, ground floor and first floor), building K3 (entrance gatehouse, 64.31 m2), building K5 (HEDNO substation, 293.26 m2) and the open-air car park. Supporting files listed include the approved coverage and general-layout drawings, ATH1-DC01 plans, an active fire-protection certificate, an installer's declaration dated 09/10/26, the HEDNO standby-generator registration, entrance/exit approvals and the environmental-terms decision 9ΚΧΧΟΡ1Κ-02Α.

The completion statement repeats that of the original notification of 10 July 2026; the construction inspection certificate itself is dated 8 July 2026 and is not separately captured. A notification of operation is filed under the notification regime before the activity starts, so it is not read as proof of operation. Capture on 26 October 2026 UTC is retrieval only.

sources.publisher: České Radiokomunikace a.s. (CRA)
sources.summary: CRA reports that it is expanding its own AI infrastructure on the NVIDIA accelerated-computing platform, offered as GPU as a service. It says CRA today operates more than twenty NVIDIA HGX B300 and DGX B300 systems, with more on the way, that the investment of hundreds of millions of crowns goes mainly into the Lužice data centre in South Moravia, where the NVIDIA infrastructure is so far concentrated and its capacity is practically always sold out, and that customers train and run models on CRA infrastructure. It closes that a further opportunity for cooperation with NVIDIA will be the Prague Gateway data centre in Jíloviště near Prague, 'where CRA is building one of the largest data centres in the region' (kde CRA staví jedno z největších datových center v regionu), with potential involvement in the AI Gigafactory project.

sources.title: Green media release: Green kauft Areal in Birr und baut digitale Infrastruktur in der Schweiz aus
sources.publisher: Green Datacenter AG / green.ch AG
sources.summary: Green's media release, datelined Lupfig, 26 October 2026, states that Green has acquired from ABB the Areal Grossacher und Grändel in Birr (canton Aargau), an area of about 250,000 m2 that ABB had held as a largely unused strategic industrial reserve, and that Green plans to develop the site in stages into a campus with data-centre infrastructure, creating additional capacity. Development is to proceed in stages on the basis of the existing Ergänzungsplan, centred on an energy-efficient data-centre campus whose waste heat is to be offered as process heat and fed into a heat network; closed-loop cooling is the design basis. Further areas for industry, commerce and public green space are foreseen, with uses to be defined with the municipality of Birr and the canton. The boilerplate says Green operates seven data centres in the greater Zurich area, has two more under construction and is planning first projects in Germany, and that its head office is in the neighbouring municipality of Lupfig. No capacity, building permit, construction start or timetable is given.
sources.date_semantics: Dated 26.10.2026 on the page (HTML time element datetime 2026-10-26) and in the dateline; listed in Green's media-release sitemap with lastmod 2026-10-26 (local green-de-sitemap-medien.xml). The release establishes an announced project as of its publication day; no physical status is stated.

sources.title: NorthC Schweiz blog: Mehr Standorte, Nähe, Resilienz: NorthC verbindet die Schweiz
sources.publisher: NorthC Schweiz AG (NorthC Datacenters)
sources.summary: NorthC's Swiss post states that NorthC operates the leading supra-regional data-centre network in Switzerland, with data centres in Münchenstein, Biel, Winterthur and Geneva (2028), and that its four carrier- and cloud-neutral data centres in Münchenstein, Biel and Winterthur are equipped for IT requirements up to AI set-ups, with almost 10,000 m2 and over 6.4 MW of power capacity in total across the Basel, Biel/Bern and Winterthur/Zurich regions, linked by a redundant network of up to 400 Gbit/s. sources.title: Telia Lietuva, AB Interim Report January-September 2026
sources.publisher: Telia Lietuva, AB
sources.summary: The issuer's nine-month interim report filed on Nasdaq Baltic. The CEO comment (page 4) states that in September 2026 an important milestone in the construction of the new data center near Vilnius was reached: the first phase, erection of the main building, was completed; the EUR 26 million project is scheduled for completion in the second quarter of 2027, after which installation and testing of the engineering and IT infrastructure systems will begin, to be completed by the end of 2028 when two initial modules with more than 400 racks will be ready for the first customers. The operations review (page 12) repeats that in September 2026 Telia Lietuva completed the first construction phase of a new Tier III standard data center near Vilnius and that construction is scheduled for completion in Q2 2027.
sources.date_semantics: Report for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, signed 'Vilnius, 21 October 2026' (PDF created 21 October 2026 17:27 EEST); 21 October 2026 is used as published_at. The exchange's own announcement timestamp could not be captured (the Nasdaq Baltic listings are script-rendered); the issuer's Q2 report, signed 16 July 2026, is recorded in the Atlas as published 17 July 2026, so the exchange release may be dated 22 October 2026. Either date postdates the 30 September 2026 observation, which follows the existing record's period-end convention (30 June 2026 from the Q2 report). Completion in Q2 2027 and the end-2028 module readiness are forecasts.
sources.personal_data_note: No names of individuals are reproduced.

sources.title: Greenergy Data Centers (MCF Group Estonia): Estonian investors raise their stake in the Hüüru data center to 42.5 percent (28 September 2026)
sources.publisher: MCF Group Estonia OÜ (Greenergy Data Centers)
sources.attribution: MCF Group Estonia OÜ / Greenergy Data Centers
sources.summary: Release datelined Tallinn, 28 September 2026, on the operator's own site (English; the Estonian original at gdc.ee, captured as local gdc-blogi-20260928-osalus.html, has the same content): Tensor Genesis (Tensor Aurora and UG Investments) has raised its stake in MCF Group Estonia, which operates the Greenergy Data Centers facility in Hüüru, from 25.55 to 42.5 percent. It states that the first part of Greenergy Data Centers designed for artificial intelligence is currently being built out (Estonian: 'ehitatakse praegu välja'), with Nebius as its tenant, that after the first phase the facility's IT load will grow to about 22 MW, and, quoting Tensor Estate's co-founder and CEO, that the first phase of the AI factory at the data center will be completed by the end of the year. MCF Group Estonia has applied to Elering to raise its grid connection to up to 200 MW. The footer gives the address Alajaama tee 1, 76911 Hüüru.
sources.date_semantics: Page 'Published 28.9.2026' and JSON-LD datePublished 2026-09-28. The present-tense statement that the first AI part is being built out is used as the observation on the publication date; it does not give the day works moved beyond site preparation. Year-end 2026 completion of the first phase and the 22 MW IT load are forecasts; the 200 MW grid application is not data-centre capacity.
sources.personal_data_note: Names of executives quoted in the release and the contact e-mail addresses and telephone numbers in the page footer are not reproduced.
